articles.title: Tiger Woods and Vanessa Trump’s business ventures: How their wealth is built through investments, real estate and major brands
articles.summary: International Sports News: Vanessa Trump and Tiger Woods have built their financial lives in very different ways. Vanessa Trump’s wealth is linked largely to her family’s invest.
articles.body: Vanessa Trump and Tiger Woods have built their financial lives in very different ways. Vanessa Trump’s wealth is linked largely to her family’s investments, inheritance, real estate and earlier modelling and business ventures.Tiger Woods, meanwhile, has created a much broader business empire through golf, sports, technology, hospitality and investments. Woods has turned his success on the golf course into a major commercial portfolio. Vanessa has also invested in property and previously launched her own handbag line.Tiger Woods and Vanessa Trump’s business venturesTiger Woods has created one of the most diversified business portfolios in professional sport. His commercial interests are largely connected to his parent enterprise, TGR Ventures.One of his major ventures is TGR Design. The company focuses on golf course design and has worked on several high-profile projects. Woods has also expanded into sports entertainment through TMRW Sports.TMRW Sports was co-founded by Woods, Rory McIlroy and Mike McCarley. The company helped create TGL, a technology-driven indoor golf league. Woods is also connected to Jupiter Links Golf Club, one of the teams competing in TGL.Woods has also entered the fashion industry. His Sun Day Red apparel and footwear brand was launched in 2024 in partnership with TaylorMade. The brand is aimed at the premium golf and lifestyle market.His business portfolio also includes PopStroke. The company combines mini-golf, dining and entertainment. Its putting courses feature designs associated with TGR Design.Woods is also involved in hospitality through The Woods Jupiter in Florida. The venue combines food, drinks and sports entertainment.His investment portfolio extends into technology and fitness. Woods has backed companies including Whoop, Hyperice, GOLF+, Future and Full Swing Golf. These investments have given him exposure to wearable technology, recovery products, virtual reality and golf simulation.Real estate is another major part of Woods’ wealth. His most famous property is his oceanfront compound in Jupiter Island, Florida. He bought the land for around $40 million in 2006 and developed a huge private estate.Vanessa Trump’s financial story is different.Her late father, attorney Charles Haydon, reportedly invested around $1 million for a 30% stake in Rao’s Specialty Foods. The company produced the popular Rao’s Homemade pasta sauce.When Rao’s Specialty Foods was sold in 2017 for $415 million, the investment reportedly generated a substantial financial windfall for the family.Vanessa also had her own business venture. Between 2010 and 2013, she operated La Poshett, a handbag and accessories line.Real estate remains another important part of her financial portfolio. She purchased a property in Jupiter, Florida, in 2019 for about $1.3 million. The home was later renovated and has been reported to be worth more than $2.5 million.She has also been linked to a luxury Manhattan apartment valued at around $3 million.While Vanessa does not appear to operate a major active business empire like Woods, her wealth is connected to inheritance, property and investments. Woods, on the other hand, has continued expanding his commercial interests across golf, technology, hospitality, media and lifestyle brands.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Reitz football pull away in Week 3 win against Jasper
articles.summary: Reitz found success early and never looked back in its Week 3 win against Jasper. Here's how they secured a third-straight dominant victory.
articles.body:
See our best photos of Jasper against Reitz in high school football week 3

EVANSVILLE — After what initially looked like a close encounter was brewing between Jasper and Reitz, the latter pulled away and won in a blowout. Again.

It finished 56-21 at the Reitz Bowl on September 4.

For Jasper coach Derek Hart, his outlook was plain and simple.

"We got whooped," Hart said. "We talked all week about taking care of the football, and in the first drive of the game, we throw a pick. We struggled defensively, but we have to compete better than we did tonight."

This week's heat wave affected both teams' preparation for Week 3, but Hart would not use that as an excuse. His group got outplayed.

The pick Hart was referring to was a Jaxson Woodring interception early in the first quarter. It was one of two takeaways for the junior — the other being a scoop and score for a touchdown in the fourth quarter. Reitz had three turnovers altogether, as E'Ani Clardy caught an interception in the third quarter.

It was the second-consecutive week for Woodring to find the end zone defensively. He said it is a result of what his defense is doing through three weeks.

"I'm doing everything I can, but it's a team sport," Woodring said. "Defense is doing everything right, we just come ready to play."

It was another challenging quarterback for the Panthers to deal with in Week 3. Jasper's Jaylen Maners is an all-state quarterback with the ability to attack defenses through the air and on the ground. He put it all together as he willed the Wildcats down the field for a touchdown before halftime.

Still, Reitz made the plays needed to halt the Wildcats on multiple possessions. Panthers coach Cory Brunson was pleased with the effort.

"(Maners) still did a lot of good things that we have to get better in stopping," Brunson said. "But it was another team effort."

The Reitz offense impressed, surpassing the 40-point mark for the third week in a row.

Amyr Wilford will get the praise (two touchdowns vs Jasper) for what he brings to the field every week, and deservedly so. He had a minor scare Friday, though, when limped off the field in the second half. He did return shortly thereafter.

His fellow sophomore, quarterback Hunter Moers, has also been effective. Moers has been an efficient operator to open the season. Few balls are hitting the ground.

Moers finished the game with 4 touchdowns. Three went to Mason Bailey, who showcased his ability to separate and run after catch. The other went to Lee Steele on a trick play in the second quarter.

From the offensive line to the skill positions, Moers said everything seems to be meshing on offense. And through three weeks as the starter for Reitz, he is feeling well acclimated to the new role.

"It's going well," Moers said. "Just continuously watching film, working hard every day in practice and making sure I'm on with my guys."

In Week 4, the Panthers head to Bundrant Stadium to face North, who emerged from its Week 3 matchup at Harrison with a 22-20 win. Although the Huskies are 1-2, it remains a tough challenge to mitigate the threat Jayden Jones and Hunter McKinney bring as a quarterback/running back duo.

"We have to work hard at practice this week," Woodring said. "Take every day serious, and every rep. We'll see how it goes."

Brunson said North should be undefeated. He expects a tough test at Bundrant.

As for Jasper, a trip to Bosse awaits in Week 4. Hart hopes for a response from the Wildcats, as was the mentality heading into their Week 2 win against Harrison.

articles.title: Marion Harding football gives coach the fast start he craved in Week 3 win
articles.summary: Marion Harding wanted to start fast in its first road trip of the football season and did just that at Bellefontaine on Sept. 4.
articles.body:
BELLEFONTAINE — C.J. Westler asked his team for it all week, and they delivered.

"Our goal all week was a fast start. I think we did that," he said.

Marion Harding scored on its first two possessions of the game, and the defense took care of the rest in a 14-7 road victory Sept. 4 at Bellefontaine in a Week 3 high school football game.

"We moved the ball a little bit in the second half, but we just couldn't finish drives," Westler said. "They kind of caught us off guard going tempo on that first drive (of the second half when Bellefontaine scored). They ran it right down the field.

"Our defense responded. We made a lot of mistakes, but they played extremely hard. We made a couple fourth-down stands down in the red zone."

It took just five plays and 1:22 off the clock to start the game with a 7-0 lead. Dez Feliciano hit Jaden Jordan for a 38-yard pass play and Jackson Payne for an 11-yard gain before striking with Reggie Walker for a 13-yard score.

On the next possession, it looked like Feliciano scored on a 97-yard keeper, bouncing off tackles down the field, but a holding call brought it back. Nevertheless, the Presidents engineered a 14-play drive that ate nearly six minutes off the clock. Feliciano earned that second touchdown on a 2-yard run.

"Our kids play extremely hard, but we told them last week that playing hard is not good enough. You don't want to be the team that says, 'Man they play hard, but they don't win,'" Westler said.

Bellefontaine opened the second half with an 11-play, 60-yard drive that Dillon Jones finished on a 1-yard run. That cut the Harding lead to 14-7, but that was the only blemish by the Prexy D.

In the first half, the Presidents stopped Bellefontaine on a fourth-and-goal from the 3, then on the next series stopped it again on fourth-and-goal from the 5. Payne picked off a pass to thwart a third drive.

In the second half after the BHS touchdown, Harding's defense posted back-to-back 3-and-outs, then stopped the hosts on a fourth-and-4 from the Harding 44. The defense put the game away when Sean Kelly recovered a fumble with 1:37 left.

"In years past, this is the kind of game we would have let slip away. I feel like we're finally starting to turn that corner to where we're able to weather the storm and be able to finish it off," Westler said.

Both teams finished with 13 first downs, but Harding outgained its opponent 351 to 232 in total yards.

Feliciano was 9-for-24 passing for 129 yards, plus ran it 16 times for 75 yards. McGary finished with 107 yards on 12 carries, and Shaukoyre Jackson ran eight times for 36 yards. Walker made four catches for 43 yards and Jordan three catches for 70. Quincy Carter paced the defense with 6.5 tackles, and Kolten Sibrel added 4.5. Noah Shockley and Maddox Moran shared a crucial sack in the second half.

articles.title: 3 biggest takeaways from Oklahoma's dominant win over UTEP
articles.summary: Three key takeaways from Oklahoma's dominant season-opening win over UTEP.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners kicked off the 2026 college football season with a dominant 51-0 win over the University of Texas at El Paso Miners. The Sooners dominated this one from start to finish, outscoring the Miners 21-0 in the first quarter.

While it was a great win to start the season, with both the offense and defense having their moments, it wasn't all perfect. Here are the three biggest takeaways from the Sooners' win on Friday.

The run game is heading in the right direction

This was one of the biggest topics of the offseason. The Sooners showed early that they wanted to focus on the run game. They tried it from all different looks, including under center. But the run game was more like death by a thousand cuts than a dominant showing. Oklahoma ran for 170 yards and two scores on 4.4 yards per carry, but only two runs topped over 20 yards. Lloyd Avant led the way with 79 yards on 15 carries.

The Sooners just consistently were eeking out four or five yards a carry. That's not bad, but it wasn't as dominant as it could have been. Now, it's important to point out: three projected starters on the offensive line missed most of the game. Center Jake Maikkula and guard Ryan Fodje both missed the game due to injury. Tackle Michael Fasusi played sparingly, likely wanting to make sure he stayed healthy.

The defense still has some things to clean up

The Sooners' defense on paper looked like it played a dominant game. It pitched a shutout and allowed less than 200 yards of total offense. The defense also forced two turnovers. But UTEP had some success. The Miners got into Oklahoma territory multiple times, but missed three field goals.

The biggest issue was missing tackles. The Sooners missed far too many tackles and gave up outside containment multiple times. Oklahoma allowed 112 yards on the ground, including a 51-yard run by Raymond Moore II. Quarterback EJ Colson Jr. also had some success, especially early in the game.

It was still a good performance, and you never want to be upset by a shutout. Oklahoma had four sacks and 10 tackles for loss. The Sooners led the nation in both stats last season. Still, it felt like the Sooners left a lot on the table that they will have to clean up before facing the Michigan Wolverines next weekend. Fans shouldn't be worried yet with Brent Venables at the helm.

The tight end room could be a real strength

If there was one position group that provided an especially encouraging glimpse of what's possible this season, it was the tight ends. The Sooners consistently ran 12 personnel on offense, meaning two tight ends. That was typically Hayden Hansen and Rocky Beers. They even went 14 personnel at one point. Jack Van Dorselaer and Trynae Washington played a role early.

On top of that, the tight ends played a role in the passing game. Beers had two catches for 43 yards and a touchdown. That includes his 40-yard touchdown. Hansen also had one catch for 15 yards in the game.

It's obviously important not to overreact to what happened against UTEP. The competition gets considerably tougher from here. But the way Oklahoma used its tight ends suggests this could be a much more involved position group than it was a year ago. And that's encouraging for an offense that is trying to become more physical while taking some pressure off quarterback John Mateer.

For an opener, Oklahoma got almost everything it needed from Friday night. Mateer completed 11-of-17 passes for 225 yards and three touchdowns, Isaiah Sategna delivered an 88-yard punt return for a score and the defense pitched a shutout.

Now comes the real test. Michigan will expose weaknesses that UTEP couldn't, particularly on the road and in the trenches. If Oklahoma can carry the physicality it showed Friday while eliminating the missed tackles and continuing to develop its rushing attack, the Sooners will enter Ann Arbor with considerably more confidence than they had a week ago.

articles.title: LSU leaves Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris off roster as SEC punishment threats linger
articles.summary: LSU will not roster NFL camp participants Zxavian Harris and Dae'Quan Wright as the SEC continues to battle in courts.
articles.body:
LSU is finding that the problem with a declawed cat is that it can still bare its teeth.

As the school continues to fight a protracted battle against the SEC that seems to be destined for the courts, the Tigers' roster for the season opener was reportedly missing a few notable names, per Pete Thamel: NFL camp participants Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, who were expected to be rostered after being granted a preliminary injunction by a Louisiana judge on Sept. 3. The SEC later issued a statement that it expects schools to follow its rules.

The move comes in the wake of the SEC threatening dramatic action against teams rostering players who were previously on NFL rosters, including:

50% of season suspension for head coaches

50% of that sport's annual operating budget

SEC voting privileges revoked on some matters

While it was initially reported the conference's charter members unanimously voted in approval of the punishments, it was later reported LSU abstained from the vote.

In an interesting twist, LSU only filled 103 of its 105 roster spots, leaving a path for Wright and Harris to be added at a later date.

Why were Zxavian Harris, Dae'Quan Wright left off LSU's roster?

Although the ruling from Judge William Jorden opened the door for LSU to roster Wright and Harris, there is a tremendous amount of scrutiny surrounding the two names.

LSU has been under heavy fire for considering carrying the two on its 105-man roster, and the SEC has promised steep punishments against teams trying to play players who were previously with NFL teams. In a move that preempted Jorden's ruling, the SEC filed suit against LSU and Lane Kiffin, claiming that its First Amendment rights were being violated by LSU playing the players at direct odds with SEC rules.

With that in mind, though the preliminary injunction prevents the NCAA, SEC, or LSU from taking action against the players, the threat of retribution from the SEC is still very real, and if LSU rosters Harris and Wright it runs the risk of retroactive punishment in all games they participate in. In other words, they're being left off until there's more clarity.

Can Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris be added to LSU roster later?

With two roster spots open, LSU is sending a clear message it wants Wright and Harris on the team. The two are enrolled at LSU, so they can be added later.

However, with the amount of uncertainty hanging in the air over this situation, LSU is clearly trying to slow-play it until it knows it can get away with having the two on the team. It's a half-measure, to be sure, but ultimately the door is very much open to add Wright and Harris later.

A first home game in three weeks brings a familiar opponent for Brighton, who have not lost to Leeds United at the Amex Stadium in over a decade.

Fabian Hurzeler's side will look to bounce back from their first defeat of the season, having been beaten 4-3 at Chelsea last time out. Hurzeler has praised Daniel Farke's Leeds as a "hardworking team" who "don't give away a lot of chances," and expects Saturday's game to be "a fight" despite his own side's attacking pedigree so far this season.

Jack Hinshelwood, Yankuba Minteh, Kaoru Mitoma, Mats Wieffer, Stefanos Tzimas and Evan Ferguson are all sidelined through injury, with Wieffer not expected back until after next month's international break. Georginio Rutter and Yasin Ayari are both doubts having missed the defeat at Chelsea, though Hurzeler sounded encouraged about Ayari's chances of involvement, saying of his ankle knock: "He could finish the game against Tromso, so hopefully it's not that bad."

Costinha could be handed his first start at right-back in Wieffer's absence, while new signings Chema Andres and Femi Azeez are both in contention to feature, most likely from the bench. Pascal Gross, who scored and set up a goal against Chelsea, continues in midfield and is closing in on 250 Premier League appearances. Charalampos Kostoulas remains an option up front should Rutter not be risked from the start.

Crystal Palace will look to get their first win of the new Premier League season when they take on Fulham on Saturday at the Craven Cottage.

Crystal Palace are enduring a tough start under new manager Pierre Sage, as they are hunting for their first points. The Eagles opened their campaign with a 2–0 loss away to Everton before suffering a heavy 4–1 defeat at home to Manchester City. Defensively fragile, Palace have conceded six goals in two games. Their solitary goal so far this term came courtesy of an own goal, highlighting a critical lack of cutting edge up front.

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage faces a far more challenging selection dilemma as he hunts for his first points of the new campaign with a heavily depleted squad.

The Eagles will be entirely without star striker Jean-Philippe Mateta, who has been ruled out for roughly three weeks after sustaining a hamstring injury.

Ismaïla Sarr is also sidelined with a groin issue, having missed recent training following a collapsed transfer move to Liverpool.

Furthermore, defender Chadi Riad remains sidelined long-term with a severe knee injury. On a brighter note, Sage could hand debuts to a wave of late transfer arrivals.

Ben Chilwell, Honest Ahanor, Quinten Timber, and Darío Osorio have all trained with the first team and are fully eligible to feature. Osorio, in particular, is heavily tipped to receive early minutes out wide to help offset Palace's attacking absences.

articles.title: Manchester City vs Coventry City – Match preview and team news
articles.summary: Manchester City can extend a perfect start to the season when they host newly promoted Coventry City at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. Enzo Maresca’s side h...
articles.body:
Manchester City can extend a perfect start to the season when they host newly promoted Coventry City at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday.

Enzo Maresca's side have won both of their opening matches, while Frank Lampard's Coventry are yet to open their account for either points or goals.

This will be the two clubs' first meeting since March 2002, when City won 4-2 at Maine Road with both sides then in the second tier. Their history in the top flight is more competitive than Saturday's odds suggest, though: Coventry are unbeaten in their last eight Premier League meetings with City (W4 D4), a run stretching back to the 1992-93 season, when City won both fixtures.

Both sides overhauled their squads before Tuesday's transfer deadline: City completed a club-record £125m deal for Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea, while Coventry added eleven new signings across the summer as they returned to the top flight after 25 years away.

Manchester City vs Coventry City – Match preview and team news

Last meeting: Manchester City 4-2 Coventry City (Second Division, March 2002)

Jeremy Doku remains sidelined with a calf injury, but Matheus Nunes has recovered from a muscle problem and is available again. Enzo Maresca confirmed deadline-day signing Enzo Fernandez is ready to make his full debut, while fellow new arrival Iliman Ndiaye is also available for selection. Ayyoub Bouaddi, who impressed off the bench last time out, could be handed a first start.

Haji Wright remains a long-term absentee, while Sidiki Cherif is a doubt, though Frank Onyeka has recovered from a hip problem and is available. Bobby Thomas is expected to continue at centre-back having come off with cramp against Hull, with Frank Lampard considering a switch to a five-man defence. Ephron Mason-Clark is set to partner Taiwo Awoniyi in attack, though his involvement is subject to a final fitness check.

Manchester City have made the perfect start under new head coach Enzo Maresca, beating Bournemouth 2-1 before winning 4-1 at Crystal Palace, with Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland scoring twice apiece. City also lead the Premier League for successful passes and passing accuracy so far this season, reflecting the possession-based approach Maresca has already instilled.

Coventry have lost both of their opening fixtures without scoring, beaten 3-0 by Arsenal before a narrow 1-0 home defeat to Hull City. It is a daunting start to their first top-flight campaign in 25 years, coming immediately after winning last season's Championship title, and Frank Lampard has stressed the need for his players to adjust their mindset.

Maresca has praised the impact of a busy transfer window, thanking the club's ownership after a summer of significant squad turnover. The head coach has stressed the need for focus despite City's status as overwhelming favourites, warning that games against promoted sides "can be tricky" if his side are not fully switched on.

Jeremy Doku remains sidelined with a calf injury sustained in the Community Shield defeat to Arsenal and has missed both of City's opening league fixtures. There is better news on Matheus Nunes, who has recovered from a muscle problem that forced him to sit out the win at Crystal Palace and is available for selection again.

articles.title: Williams sisters exit US Open but excite - what does future hold?
articles.summary: Serena and Venus Williams may have lost in their US Open doubles return, but the veteran pair proved they can still compete on an entertaining night in New Y...
articles.body:
Rarely has a women's doubles first-round match headlined the US Open night session - but the Williams sisters are like no other pairing.

Serena and Venus Williams might have a combined age of 90, but their star remains undimmed. Neither does their ability to compete at the highest level when they are in tandem.

Even though the superstar siblings - aged 44 and 46 - lost on their highly-anticipated Grand Slam return, their performance in a narrow defeat by 14th seeds Hao-Ching Chan and Maya Joint led to an entertaining night in New York.

A packed Arthur Ashe Stadium roared on the American icons as they looked on course for a memorable win - but ultimately fell short in a 6-3 6-7 (6-8) 7-6 (10-7) loss.

"It was unbelievable how competitive that was," said former American player-turned-commentator Chanda Rubin, who lost to the Williams sisters in the 1999 US Open doubles final.

"After the first set you wondered if Serena and Venus would be able to find their mojo - but, boy, they did."

Four years after they last appeared on Ashe, the Williams sisters were given a rapturous reception as they strode onto a court where they have won eight singles titles between them and two doubles titles together.

The decibel levels were rarely matched in an underwhelming first set for the home favourites, but the noise quickly returned when they rallied in the second set.

The atmosphere became muted as the decider seemed to run away from them at 4-1 down, before they showed indomitable spirit - a hallmark of their extraordinary careers - to take their opponents into a first-to-10 match tie-break.

Racing into a 5-0 lead put the Williams sisters firmly on course to reach the second round, only for Chan and Joint to fight back - with the help of a double fault from each opponent.

Despite the initial despondency of the home fans, the volume was turned back up when the American pair were given a fond farewell - with everyone left wondering what the future holds for them both.

Serena hinted earlier this week she wanted to play singles again in an interview with Good Morning America, while Venus said after her singles exit on Monday that she should not "have to" think about her future beyond the doubles.

The questions about what happens next were not addressed by the pair following Friday's match. The sisters decided they were "not available" to speak to the media, US Open organisers said.

For once, the 20,000-odd fans on a packed Arthur Ashe Stadium sat quietly engrossed during points.

The sight of the Williams sisters back on court together at the US Open - possibly for the final time - commanded ultimate respect from a chatty crowd known to let their attention wander.

The siblings changed the face of the sport when they emerged as precocious teenagers in the 1990s, going on to dominate the sport with a combined 30 Grand Slam singles titles and 14 doubles victories as a pair.

Three decades later, the sport remains captivated by them.

Serena, a record 23-time Grand Slam women's singles champion, coming out of retirement this summer sparked excitement among those who saw them in their prime and those too young to have witnessed it.

Seven-time major winner Venus has never "evolved away" from the sport - the words chosen by her younger sister when she last played in 2022 - but instead continued her career with the help of sporadic wildcards.

While that has proved controversial in some quarters, there were few objections about the sisters being invited to play once again at Flushing Meadows.

Their planned return at Wimbledon was scuppered by the knee injury which Serena suffered in her singles match there - ironically a defeat by 20-year-old Joint - before they finally reunited at the WTA event in Cincinnati.

The comeback ended in a match tie-break defeat by Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk and her American partner Peyton Stearns, with the same fate befalling them in New York.

When the Williams sisters last played on Ashe four years ago, they suffered a straight-set defeat by Czech pair Lucie Hradecka and Linda Noskova in the first round.

It looked like being a similar fate as they meekly surrendered the first set against Chan and Joint, then batted off four break points in the fifth and seventh games of the second set.

But once Serena upped her level to match her impressive sister, they managed to switch the momentum back in their favour and level the match.

An absorbing contest featuring some sensational points saw the Americans fight back again in the decider, only to falter from a commanding lead in the tie-break.

Overall it was a more than credible performance from the veteran pair. Their solid groundstrokes, sharp movement and never-say-die attitude caused problems for their opponents, who deserve huge credit for staying focused in a partisan environment.

"The atmosphere was surreal," said Joint.

"It was something we've never experienced before, and to play against such legends of the game was super special."

articles.title: 'Los Gallos' se conjuran en Valencia para acabar con el maleficio
articles.standfirst: El equipo español de SailGP no se metió en una final del Gran Premio de España durante los cuatro años que se celebró en Cádiz. Llega mejor que nunca para acabar con la mala racha
articles.summary: El equipo español de SailGP no se metió en una final del Gran Premio de España durante los cuatro años que se celebró en Cádiz. Llega mejor que nunca para acabar con la mala racha
articles.body: El equipo español de SailGP quiere romper el maleficio en Valencia. Durante los cuatro años que Cádiz fue la sede del Gran Premio de España, a ‘Los Gallos’ se les resistió entrar en la final ante su público y luchar por el volante de campeón que se entrega en cada G.P. con los colores de la bandera del país anfitrión. Pero no es sólo un reto de los españoles; sólo Australia ha conseguido ganar ante los suyos (2019, 2022 y 2024) a lo largo de las seis temporadas. ‘Los Gallos’ se han conjurado para cambiar las estadísticas en Valencia. “Tenemos la espinita de ganar en casa y aunque sabemos que es súper difícil, estamos más preparados que nunca para ello”, asegura Diego Botín, el piloto del equipo español. Y tiene razón el cántabro porque los números no engañan. Llegan a Valencia segundos en la general del Rolex SailGP Championship, a 14 puntos de los australianos y tras haber subido al podio en los siete Grandes Premios que han navegado esta temporada: dos triunfos, dos segundos puestos y tres terceros. Se han convertido en un referente de la flota, que ahora les estudia en vídeos y consulta sus datos, ya que en SailGP la data de los 13 barcos es compartida. “Miran sobre todo lo relativo a nuestras remontadas. Nosotros tenemos ahora este nivel gracias a que hemos estado mucho tiempo analizando a otros mejores”, reconoce Botín. Este fin de semana se esperan vientos térmicos ligeros, una condiciones que suponen un reto para que los F50 se eleven sobre el mar. Joel Rodríguez, el controlador de vuelo español, nos da la clave: “El barco que consiga estar foileando el máximo tiempo va a tener muchas opciones. Hay que buscar el viento limpio y estar bien técnicamente para navegar rápido”. Para Botín y Trittel, campeones olímpicos, mundiales y europeos, es la única espinita que les queda. “Ya hemos ganado también SailGP –en 2024– y lo que tenemos pendiente en nuestra carrera deportiva es meternos en una final en casa y ganarla. Soñamos con darle una alegría a la Marea Roja (los aficionados españoles). Llegamos en nuestro mejor momento”, recuerda Trittel, trimmer de ala. La flota se divide en dos grupos y ‘Los Gallos’ se van a jugar este fin de semana el billete a la final –pasan los dos primeros de cada grupo– con Canadá, Francia, Dinamarca, Alemania y EE.UU. ¿A qué se debe su regularidad esta temporada? Todos responden lo mismo: la unión del equipo. Todos sus componentes inciden en ella y en la apuesta a largo plazo que hicieron desde el inicio, cuando eran el equipo más joven de la flota y pocos apostaban por ellos. Quienes sí lo han hecho es Quantum Pacific, accionista del Atlético de Madrid y de la gestora del Movistar Team de ciclismo. La compra del equipo español garantiza su continuidad en SailGP. "Cuando yo llegué hace tres años el objetivo era sobrevivir", recuerda Antonio Alquézar, CEO del equipo español. "Nos da esa tranquilidad que necesitamos para hacer crecer el proyecto y pensar en el futuro y no estar cada día pensando en a ver si va a ser el último", dice Nicole Van der Velden, la estratega del equipo.

articles.title: ‘Absolutely Sick of This’ – Venus, Serena Williams’ ‘Unprofessional’ Media No-Show at US Open Leaves Tennis World Fuming
articles.summary: Venus and Serena Williams reunited for the women’s doubles event at the 2026 US Open, four years after they last took the court together in New York, when Se...
articles.body:
Venus and Serena Williams reunited for the women's doubles event at the 2026 US Open, four years after they last took the court together in New York, when Serena was competing in what was expected to be her final professional tournament.

The pair came agonizingly close to pulling off a remarkable win, but they ultimately fell short against Chan Hao-Ching and Maya Joint. However, it was the decision the Williams sisters made after the defeat that has drawn scrutiny from the tennis community.

Why Venus and Serena Williams Are Facing Criticism After Their US Open Exit

Venus and Serena Williams made a slow start to their opening women's doubles match, as Chan and Joint clinched the first set 6-3. However, the American pair delighted the passionate home crowd by edging a closely contested second-set tiebreak to force a decider.

Despite trailing 1-4 in the third set, the Williams sisters fought back strongly to level the score and send the match into a super tiebreak. The duo appeared poised for an impressive comeback win after racing to a 5-0 lead, but several costly errors allowed Chan and Joint to bounce back and secure a 6-3, 6-7(6), 7-6 [10-7] victory.

Despite the narrow loss, Venus and Serena were all smiles as they acknowledged the crowd's cheers while leaving Arthur Ashe Stadium.

However, their post-match thoughts remained a mystery, as tennis journalist Ben Rothenberg revealed that the US Open had informed reporters that the Williams sisters would not be available for the customary post-match press conference. Rothenberg added that he was far from surprised by the decision.

"From the U.S. Open: "Serena and Venus Williams will not be available for press tonight." Deeply unsurprising," Rothenberg posted.

Fellow journalist James Gray also expressed his lack of surprise at the decision when asked whether he was expecting anything different, commenting , "Well no, I suppose not."

Meanwhile, fans criticized Venus and Serena Williams for not adhering to the rules about addressing the press, with one fan even suggesting that they should forfeit their prize money.

"I understand its their choice but they should need to forfeit their prize money. Press is part of being a professional athlete," one fan commented .

"Good riddance at this stage. I'm not press but I'm absolutely sick of this "rules don't apply to us" attitude. Four wild cards between them this US Open and they basically giving a big middle finger to the tournament and the press @usopen," said another .

Others perceived the duo to be "sore losers" and "unprofessional."

"Not surprising at all. Always have been sore losers," a fan wrote .

"They've never been good sports, why would they change now? I'd love to what Billie Jean King thinks about these no-shows from them. Very unprofessional after so many players before them did all the work," another fan chimed in .

"Win and they wouldn't shut up….lose and it's unavailable… 🤔," a user posted .

In addition to her women's doubles campaign, Serena Williams also competed in the mixed doubles event with Carlos Alcaraz. The high-profile duo triumphed over Erin Routliffe and Lloyd Glasspool in their opening match before losing to Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli in the quarterfinals.

Meanwhile, Venus Williams had entered the singles draw as a wild card, facing Sofia Kenin in the first round. Although Venus held seven set points in the second set, she failed to convert any of them, allowing Kenin to secure a 6-2, 7-6(6) victory.

articles.title: Super League: St Helens 'need a big clear out' as team's recruitment questioned after missing play-offs
articles.summary: St Helens missed out on Super League play-offs for the first time in the club's history after 48-10 defeat by Leigh Leopards; Round 26 of Super League continues on Saturday September 5, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
St Helens' standing at seventh on the Super League ladder for the 2026 season was confirmed on Friday night after they were thumped 48-10 by Leigh Leopards, while Hull KR's 36-6 win against Huddersfield confirmed the top six.

It was Saints' seventh defeat in their last 10 matches and second heavy loss in a row, having suffered a 28-point reverse to Leeds a week ago.

O'Carroll is due to be replaced by former Brisbane Broncos and Australia head coach Kevin Walters ahead of the 2027 season, and the experienced coach will hope to galvanise the Saints back to their best next season.

But eyebrows have been raised over the team's recruitment decisions this year, with the club also struggling with a big injury crisis. At one stage in July, 16 players were sidelined with injuries.

Paul Rowley stepped down as the Saints coach that same month. Saints had been six points behind league leaders Leeds Rhinos at the time, but had suffered a 46-0 demolition by Toulouse earlier in July - the first time the club have gone scoreless at home in a league match since 1980.

The Saints, who won four titles in a row between 2019 and 2022, have experienced a sudden slump, and questions are being raised over the club's recruitment.

"Nothing is given in sport," Jamie Jones-Buchanan said on Sky Sports .

"You certainly can't copy and paste from one generation to another because context is king. St Helens probably need a clear out.

"They have some exceptional young talents coming through, but they're arriving at the wrong time, not having the best of experiences.

"Older players there too, who have maybe stayed a bit too long. Contextually, there are some players playing out of position.

"Tristan Sailor and Jack Welsby were really good against Leigh Leopards, you see moments of genius within it. But it's where they are playing and how it all fits together. The jigsaw has just not been great for St Helens."

Over the off-season, St Helens added experienced Australian players Shane Wright, Jacob Host and David Klemmer, while Jackson Hastings and Joe Shorrocks also arrived.

Saints also signed Daniel Suluka-Fifita midway through the campaign, but have struggled to make more acquisitions due to salary cap constraints.

It came after players including Konrad Hurrell, Morgan Knowles, Moses Mbye and Joe Bennison, left over the off-season, while Kyle Feldt was released mid-season.

The club has announced one new signing for the 2027 season, with Solomona Faataape joining from Catalans.

Sky Sports pundit and St Helens legend Jon Wilkin believes they have not replaced like-for-like and have made "short-term" recruitment choices.

"I've said it a number of times but Saints' recruitment has been shocking," Wilkin said.

"It's been terrible. They've made convenient and short-term recruitment choices. They've not replaced like-for-like and they need to rethink their recruitment strategy.

"There's a lot of young guys who have gone out into Super League who aren't ready. I'm loving that, it is great for them and for their future.

"But the reason they're out there was because you had an old squad at the start of the year that wasn't durable enough to get through a year, and then you signed shoddy replacements for guys who moved on.

"That's why young guys are having to put a Saints shirt on and are getting flogged by Leigh.

"I'm buying the message that it's all positive: 'Hey, we've got a great youth system and some young lads are getting a chance.' But if you look at the underlying reason why they are getting a chance, that's the issue. It's the root cause of their problem, sloppy recruitment over a period of three or four years."

O'Carroll: Missing out on play-offs disappointing

Reflecting on his side's season, and missing out on a spot in the Play-Offs, O'Carroll admitted that learning from this adversity may help his team move forwards in the future.

"I've just mentioned it to the group - it's obviously really disappointing," O'Carroll said after Friday's match.

"It doesn't sit well with me that I've been a part of that, I won't shy away from it.

"This group has had a lot of success, consistent success, so to experience a bit of adversity is good in some respects.

"Moving on now, I feel the conversations with Eamon and Abi, they have absolute clarity in terms of what needs to be done and I've every confidence they'll do that.

"For Kevin Walters to come in, it's probably a great time to come in now and for the club to accelerate forward."

articles.title: Alcaraz, Sabalenka into US Open last 16 as Williams sisters lose on return
articles.summary: Alcaraz beat China’s Wu Yibing 6-3, 6-4, 6-1, while Sabalenka defeated Kamilla Rakhimova 6-3, 6-4.
articles.body:
Defending singles champions Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka have sailed into the last 16 of the US Open as tennis icons Serena and Venus Williams suffered an agonising defeat on their long-awaited return to Grand Slam doubles.

Alcaraz, coming off a four-month injury absence, beat China’s Wu Yibing 6-3, 6-4, 6-1 on Friday to book his place in the fourth round, while Sabalenka was similarly dominant in a 6-3, 6-4 defeat of Kamilla Rakhimova.

Alcaraz will face 20th-seeded American Tommy Paul for a place in the quarterfinals after Paul beat 15th-seeded Alexander Bublik 6-4, 3-6, 6-7 (4/7), 6-1, 6-3.

“The way he plays is unbelievable, the rhythm he has on every shot – forehand, backhand,” Alcaraz said of Wu. “His balls skid a lot on the court and, for me, it’s really difficult to control sometimes.

“But I think I stayed there. I played aggressive. I played smart in the toughest moments.”

Wu recovered an early break in each of the first two sets, but Alcaraz pocketed both with breaks in the final games, and after saving a pair of break points in the first game of the third, the Spaniard rolled home.

“I think my level is really good,” he said. “I’ve got into the rhythm of the competition. I’m getting there.”

World number one Sabalenka did not face a break point in her dismissal of Rakhimova, firing 29 winners with 10 aces.

The numbers did not tell the whole tale of a match that saw 92nd-ranked Rakhimova challenge Sabalenka in a second-set slugfest.

Sabalenka was also unimpressed by the pervasive smell of marijuana – an increasingly common issue at the US Open – wafting down from the stands during her match.

“It’s a bit tricky to handle that smell while you’re trying to compete at your best,” said Sabalenka, who at one point complained to the umpire about the issue.

Sabalenka, who must repeat as champion to have a chance of remaining number one, next faces Taylor Townsend, the 96th-ranked American who beat 15th-seeded Russian Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-7 (3/7), 6-3.

With Alcaraz and Sabalenka among the early starters, all eyes on the evening session were on the Williams sisters, partnering in a Grand Slam doubles event for the first time since 2022.

The duo returned to the US Open stage comes after 23-time Grand Slam singles champion Serena came out of a four-year retirement to play at Wimbledon.

But the most famous sister act in tennis – who won 14 Grand Slam doubles titles together along with three Olympic gold medals – were beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6/8), 7-6 (10/7) by 14th seeds Chan Hao-ching of Taiwan and Australia’s Maya Joint in a marathon three-hour battle.

The Williams duo had shown flashes of their brilliant best after recovering from losing the first set to level the match after taking the second set on a tie-break.

Momentum and a raucous New York crowd appeared to be carrying them towards victory after they sprinted into a 5-0 lead in the third-set tie-break. But Chan and Joint fought back superbly to erase the deficit before clinching victory.

In other singles action on Friday, third-seeded American Jessica Pegula, one of the players with a chance to knock Sabalenka off her No 1 perch, mounted a desperate fightback to beat Canadian Leylah Fernandez 1-6, 6-4, 6-3 in a battle of former finalists.

Elsewhere, Ukraine’s Marta Kostyuk beat Russian Ekaterina Alexandrova 6-3, 6-2 and American Emma Navarro upset seventh-seeded Czech Karolina Muchova 6-3, 7-5.

Back in the men’s draw, American 11th seed Frances Tiafoe was a comfortable 6-4, 6-2, 6-4 victor over Monaco’s Valentin Vacherot, seeded 22.

Tiafoe’s win earned him a last 16 showdown with Russian seventh seed Daniil Medvedev.

Medvedev was a similarly unfussy winner over French 26th seed Arthur Rinderknech, easing to a 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 win in just under two hours.

Unseeded former world number three Stefanos Tsitsipas – whose ranking has plummeted to 53 – meanwhile toppled 18th seed Jiri Lehecka, 2-6, 6-1, 7-6 (7/3), 6-1 to reach the US Open fourth round for the first time.

Tsitsipas will face American eighth seed Ben Shelton in the last 16. Shelton defeated Canada’s Denis Shapovalov 7-6 (7/3), 6-7 (5/7), 6-3, 6-4 in the late match.

articles.title: Teacher's Day: Sachin Tendulkar celebrates his 'first teacher' father Ramesh with fellowship for young doctors
articles.summary: Off the field News: Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar marked Teachers’ Day with a heartfelt tribute to his father and first mentor, Ramesh Tendulkar, while announcing the P.
articles.body: Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar marked Teachers’ Day with a heartfelt tribute to his father and first mentor, Ramesh Tendulkar, while announcing the Professor Ramesh Tendulkar Memorial Fellowship to support young doctors specialising in cleft and craniofacial care.Tendulkar took to X to reflect on the influence his father had on his life and career, stressing that his journey did not begin on a cricket field or with a coach, but at home.“When I think about the people who shaped my journey, I do not begin with a cricket ground or a coach. I begin at home,” Tendulkar wrote.Ramesh Tendulkar, a writer, poet and professor, played a crucial role in nurturing his son's passion for cricket while ensuring that the young Sachin understood the importance of character and integrity. Tendulkar recalled some of the lessons his father imparted to him during his childhood, particularly the importance of accepting failure while never compromising on honesty.“Failure is okay, but cheating is not. Never take shortcuts,” Tendulkar recalled his father telling him.'My father saw something more'Tendulkar said his father never attempted to dictate what he should become. Instead, he gave him the freedom and support to discover his own path.“I was simply a boy who loved playing cricket. My father saw something more. He did not try to decide what I should become. Instead, he gave me the space and support to discover it for myself,” he wrote.According to Tendulkar, that is the essence of a great teacher or mentor, recognising potential in someone before they are able to recognise it themselves. He also highlighted the importance of providing young people with access to mentors, coaches, education and healthcare, saying talent alone is not always enough to help someone fulfil their potential.Fellowship announced in father's memoryAs part of the Teachers’ Day tribute, Tendulkar announced the Professor Ramesh Tendulkar Memorial Fellowship in partnership with the Inga Health Foundation, a long-standing healthcare partner of the Sachin Tendulkar Foundation. Under the fellowship, one MD (Doctor of Medicine) each year will receive financial support for a year-long opportunity to specialise in cleft and craniofacial care in Srinagar.After completing the programme, the fellow will receive a certificate from the Sachin Tendulkar Foundation in recognition of their work and excellence.Tendulkar said the initiative reflects the Foundation's broader commitment to supporting healthcare professionals working in critical care while encouraging young doctors to pursue specialised fields of study.'More than a fellowship'For Tendulkar, the initiative is not merely about supporting medical education but about carrying forward his father's philosophy.“For me, this is more than a fellowship. It is a way of carrying forward something my father deeply believed in - that education creates opportunity, and that opportunity becomes truly meaningful when it is used to serve others,” he wrote.Tendulkar also spoke about the work he and his wife, Anjali, have undertaken through their foundation to expand access to sports, healthcare and education for children across India.He concluded his Teachers’ Day message by reflecting on how a teacher's influence can extend well beyond a single student.“The lessons of a teacher may begin with one student, but their influence can travel much further, from one life to another and from one generation to the next,” Tendulkar wrote.“Happy Teachers’ Day!”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lahinch is home turf for GB&I, but welcome mat not rolled out for U.S. at Walker Cup
articles.summary: The visitors, with a team packed full of talent, have arrived on Irish soil looking for a sixth victory on the spin.
articles.body:
You may have noticed in the news the other day that some 70,000 pints of Guinness were pinched during a boozy heist on a storage depot.

That mighty figure is probably still lower than the number of jars of the black stuff that will disappear in the Lahinch hostelries this weekend should GB&I beat the USA and win the Walker Cup.

There are, of course, plenty of watering holes near this wonderful stretch of west coast of Ireland linksland.

"Zero," said Scottish teenager, Connor Graham, when asked how many he'd visited during the early part of the week.

"Sunday night," he added with a smile as he mulled over the prospect of a celebratory gargle in a golfing town that would certainly embrace a home win with considerable gusto.

There's a lot of golf to be played before any pint glasses can be clinked, of course.

Check out the best photos from the 2026 Walker Cup at Lahinch

At just 19 – he may yet be asked for ID given his boyish looks – Graham is almost a gnarled veteran of the Walker Cup, This, after all, will be his third appearance in the transatlantic tussle.

The Blairgowrie youngster, who is now on a golf scholarship in the US, has been on a losing side twice and he is determined to play his part in ending the USA's dominant run.

The visitors, with a team packed full of talent, have arrived on Irish soil looking for a sixth victory on the spin.

Once the Walker Cup starts, it's crash, bang, wallop. Two days of foursomes and singles can disappear in a flash after a seemingly interminable build-up.

The GB&I players have been on site since Monday – the US even earlier – and the boys on both sides are now all like coiled springs waiting to go, well, boing.

"It's a long buildup," admitted Graham with a sigh. "Putting your feet up in the afternoons is very important after you get your work done.

"I have the experience of knowing what's going on, how busy it's going to be and how important it's going to be to conserve energy going into the first day. It's a very high level of golf and you need to bring your A game."

The weather in the run-up to this weekend's showpiece has been typically robust and the winds on the penultimate practice day would've rent the Beaufort Scale asunder.

The nooks and crannies of the Lahinch links have been well explored over the past few days and, given the gusts, the GB&I captain, Dean Robertson, opted for a less is more approach.

"We only really had one hole of practice today and rested after that," said the Scot, who is in his second stint as skipper and is keen to avenge the 17-9 defeat GBI suffered in the last meeting between the sides at Cypress Point.

"The guys were able to do exactly what they wanted to do. A few of them went to some different holes.

"Today was always going to be a day where the players could really choose themselves as to what they required, whether it was a last-minute touch-up to any area or learning a few different parts of the golf course.

"The wind could be strong throughout the weekend, but it's perfectly playable. You have to adapt, you have to improvise, you have to be able to control the ball flight in these very difficult conditions.

"It's exceptionally tiring playing in these conditions, but we are good to go."

Lahinch may be home territory for GB&I this weekend, but it'll not exactly be rolling out the welcome mat.

"I think everything is difficult," added Graham of the terrific test it provides. "Trying to hit fairways, hitting greens; all parts of the game become a lot trickier when you're out there in that wind."

The stage is perfectly set and with a 16,000 sell-out crowd over two days, it should be a cracking spectacle. The lively conditions, meanwhile, are just what Robertson had hoped for.

"I requested that the golf course should play as naturally as it could be," added Robertson, who was a Walker Cup player himself back in 1993.

"You don't have to do anything to Lahinch. It's an absolute masterpiece. I think when you come to Lahinch, you're always going to expect it to be blowing.

"Getting here in July for the South of Ireland Championship was fantastic, and they had unusual winds blowing there that came from the north, which we haven't seen.

"But the wind is going to change on Saturday and it's going to come from the south, and that's not a wind that we have seen at any time during the South of Ireland or during the practice this week. That's going to bring new challenges.

"But in terms of the weather and the wind, am I happy about it? I'm very happy about it."

articles.body:
Chance Berry's announcement arrived with a fancy graphic and a two-word caption.

Last month, the Toronto, Canada, native enrolled at DME Academy in Daytona Beach.

And it's going to change again in a matter of months, with the high school senior signing to play basketball at a power-conference university. Berry, a four-star prospect who ESPN ranks as the 50th-best player in the Class of 2027 and the sixth-best in Florida, drew one step closer to that achievement on Sept. 2.

She unveiled her top eight college choices in a social media post. The list included Arizona, Arizona State, North Carolina State, Penn State, Syracuse, Texas Tech, West Virginia and UCF.

Previously, the 5-foot-11 combo guard starred for Royal Crown Academy School in Toronto. She's resided among the top names in her recruiting class for multiple years.

In 2023 and 2024, Berry suited up for Team Canada in the FIBA U16 Americas Championship and the FIBA U17 World Cup, averaging six points per game in the latter.

In 2025, she started every contest for the All Knighters in the Overtime Select league. Her club won the title.

Berry is not a complete stranger to this state, either. Last November, she led Royal Crown to an 81-67 victory over Orlando's Academy of Central Florida in Daytona Beach. Her final stat line: 26 points and 10 rebounds.

Soon, she'll make her college decision. The early signing period opens on Nov. 11.

But before then, she'll check out Daytona a little longer.

articles.title: Browns hoping improved health can lift defensive line entering opener
articles.summary: The Browns defensive line dealt with injuries through the first half of training camp. As the opener nears, though, they're starting to get healthy.
articles.body:
BEREA ― The injury bug bit the Browns in multiple areas during the course of training camp. The area most impacted was their defensive line .

It was the worst possible group to get bitten, considering the level of importance it holds to the Browns' success. The defensive line is central to the overall defense's success, and that defense may be central to the Browns' overall success.

"Yeah, I mean, with the attack front, the D-line is always the engine," defensive tackle Mason Graham said Sept. 1. "It starts with us, it ends with us. The way we think about it is no play should get past the front four, and if it does everyone else is there to clean it up. So that's kind of what we pride ourselves on, and that's what we're looking to do this year."

Cleveland Browns vs New England Patriots: Photos from preseason game

Graham was one of the defensive linemen to miss some time in training camp, although it was only a couple of days in the first week. In the grand scheme of injuries at the position, he was an ironman compared to others.

At one point early in camp, five of the top six defensive tackles were sidelined with various injuries. The defensive end group, meanwhile, suffered a major loss during the Aug. 20 joint practice against the Buffalo Bills when Alex Wright suffered a torn Achilles.

As the season opener at the Jacksonville Jaguars closes in, that group has healed to a point where it's only down a couple of key players — Wright, obviously, and defensive tackle Kalia Davis, who's on the injured reserve list. Defensive tackle Maliek Collins was activated from the physically unable to perform list Aug. 24 after a 2025 season-ending quad injury, and defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. returned Aug. 18 from a 10-day absence.

"Oh, yeah, having our guys back, I mean, there's a reason they're all ones," Browns coach Todd Monken said Sept. 1. "There's a reason why they're paid how they're paid, and that is to play at a really high level. I've seen it when they've been out there, and it's been great having them back. I mean, their consistency over the course of time, when you have those types of players, they're going to make a play that ends a drive."

The Browns already were dealing with a new-look defensive line with defensive end Jared Verse being acquired in the trade of Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams. Wright's injury led to the signing of veteran end Derek Barnett immediately afterward, then another veteran end, Sam Williams, two days after the initial roster was set.

Hall, despite having been played tackle throughout most of his first two-plus seasons, has even worked at end the last two weeks. Adin Huntington, listed as a defensive end on the roster, has worked almost exclusively at tackle behind Graham and Collins.

That's a lot of moving parts in and out of the lineup. Hall, though, said the issue of cohesion isn't a concern.

"Yeah, I mean, just with our whole style of play, we're subbing in fresh guys," Hall said Sept. 2. "We're an attack front, so we're going balls to the wall. So you got to be able to 'next man up' or be able to play with different flavors because everybody brings a whole different taste of the game."

The defensive line personnel was a big reason why it was so important for Monken to maintain a defensive scheme at least similar to the one former defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz had run over the previous three seasons. It's what led him to bring in Mike Rutenberg, whose ties to Robert Saleh, Gus Bradley and Gregg Williams directly connect his system's to Schwartz's.

The central tenet of either scheme is, as both Graham and Hall said, an attacking defensive line. It's one that requires all four to be able to get to the quarterback and rush with borderline reckless abandon.

It's why a player like Barnett, who played for Schwartz years ago when he first came into the league with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2017, can make such a smooth transition.

"Well, again, he's played in this style of defense, so it's not that big of a transition," Monken said. "It's really not. It's really just getting used to what we call things, our terminology, and then just seeing what we have. We haven't been around Derek, and I've liked what I've seen so far."

articles.title: Ravens rookie says he'd take Baltimore backup QB over Jayden Daniels
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens rookie Ja'Kobi Lane tells Washington Commanders rookie Antonio Williams that he'd take Tyler Huntley over Jayden Daniels.
articles.body:
Many questions have surrounded Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels. Some of those questions date back to before he was drafted. His size. His durability. All of that was part of why he wasn't selected No. 1 overall in the 2024 NFL Draft.

The Commanders, though, were willing to overlook some of those questions because they saw something in Daniels. And what they saw was what the rest of us eventually saw on the field in 2024, as Daniels took the league by storm and brought Raise Hail Nation back to life.

Then came 2025. Injuries. Losses. Daniels missed time. The questions that were asked before the 2024 NFL Draft resurfaced. Now, ahead of the 2026 season, there is so much shade being thrown at Daniels that Baltimore Ravens rookie Ja'Kobi Lane told Commanders rookie Antonio Williams that he'd rather have Tyler Huntley as his quarterback than Jayden Daniels.

"And we got the best dual-threat quarterback in the league," Lane says. "What?"

"Lamar Jackson, the best in the world, are you crazy? Snoop… 5… I'm taking my 5 over your 5," Lane says. "Snoop" refers to Ravens' backup quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley.

"No, you're not," Williams replied matter-of-factly.

"Yes, I am. I'm taking Tyler Huntley over the Commanders' quarterback every time."

It's one thing for a rookie wide receiver to have the back of his quarterback, and he might have an argument if he's talking about Lamar Jackson. But Huntley? He's a career backup who barely sees the field. He's never been a full-time starter on any team he's played for. In fact, the only team that has had him on their active roster is the Ravens. The Cleveland Browns and Miami Dolphins have had him on their practice squads.

You want to talk about a major dig, a way to give Daniels fuel for the fire burning in his soul as he prepares to remind the NFL who he really is? This is a great way to do that.

If you look at Huntley's 2021 season, he played in the most games of his career that season, and compare it to Daniels' 2025 season, here's what you get:

Huntley: Seven games, 122 completions for 1,081 yards, three touchdowns, four interceptions, 18 sacks, and a quarterback rating of 76.6.

Daniels: Seven games, 114 completions for 1,262 yards, eight touchdowns, three interceptions, 18 sacks, and a quarterback rating of 88.1.

Most people will take those eight touchdowns and three interceptions over three touchdowns and four interceptions all day long. Plus, Daniels was playing through injury in some of those games. So, while Huntley is a great backup, no one will ever take that away from him; he will, in no way, shape, or form, ever be able to replace Jayden Daniels.

We get it, rookie, have your quarterback's back. But also, use some sense.

articles.title: ‘Role models’ – Serena and Venus Williams’ exit after first-round loss at US Open goes viral
articles.summary: Serena Williams and Venus Williams crashed out of the women’s doubles event at the US Open in the first round, but fans had a lot to say as they made their e...
articles.body:
Serena Williams and Venus Williams crashed out of the women's doubles event at the US Open in the first round, but fans had a lot to say as they made their exit.

Serena Williams is the greatest tennis player ever for many fans. Her older sister Venus is incredibly accomplished in her own right, the two have won numerous Grand Slam titles between them.

The sisters are legends in women's doubles as well, having won 14 Grand Slams together. At the ages of 44 and 46, they entered the 2026 US Open as well, but lost in the first round.

The Williams sisters lost to Maya Joint and Chan Hao-ching in a hard-fought match. After losing the first set, then winning the second 7-6, they lost the third set in a tiebreaker.

Tennis fans were divided as the Williams sisters walked off US Open court after loss

Considering that the Williams sisters were not available to speak with the media after their loss, their walk off the court was the last that fans saw of them.

A video of their exit went viral on social media, with fans reacting to the duo they might not see on the courts again.

"Being fit at their age and still play a bit of tennis is incredible and entertaining," one fan wrote. "You better believe they changed the sport! What the Williams sisters did for women's tennis is invaluable!" said another.

"Love these sister athletes! Role models!" a third fan wrote. Not all the reactions were positive, however. A comment read, "These privileges have got to stop in tennis. Shouldn't be getting wildcards like that."

One fan wrote, "I love them, but it is officially time for them to stop playing seriously." Another added, "Legends of the game but no more wild cards, please."

Love them or hate them, there is no disputing that the Williams sisters are among the biggest legends in tennis history. If this is the last time they walk off the court together, it was a special moment.

articles.body:
Kareem Abdul-Jabbar had the greatest weapon in the history of basketball: the Skyhook.

When he was young and springy, it was an evolving weapon, but he could really get off the ground. In his prime, it was extremely difficult to deal with, and as an old man, in basketball terms anyway, it was perfected, launched with great efficiency, and very hard to stop.

We spent a little time looking into it not too long ago and found a handful of guys who blocked it, but the list kept expanding.

And now, someone has put together perhaps the best, most complete list of players who blocked it. It includes Wilt Chamberlain, Nate Thurmond, Bill Willoughby (though his was ruled goaltending), Bill Walton, Ralph Sampson, Robert Parish, and Hakeem Olajuwon.

That may sound like a lot of guys did it, but the man played for 20 years and had it blocked far less than once a year (on average).

Apparently, Julius Erving got one too, but we can't find the video.

articles.title: Isak finally arrives as Gakpo proves value to Liverpool
articles.summary: Alexander Isak was the £125m striker who finally arrived at Liverpool by tormenting Ipswich Town - while Cody Gakpo's virtuoso performance had them giving th...
articles.body:
Alexander Isak was the £125m striker who finally arrived at Liverpool by tormenting Ipswich Town - while Cody Gakpo's virtuoso performance had them giving thanks he never left.

The nuts and bolts of a comfortable Friday in Suffolk were that Liverpool won 2-0 - thanks to two Isak goals in the first nine minutes, giving them their first Premier League victory of the season and new manager Andoni Iraola's first since succeeding the sacked Arne Slot.

Liverpool's win must be placed in the context of being against a newly promoted Ipswich Town who were game, but who shipped five goals at Manchester United last week and look ripe for the picking against attacking quality.

The wider significance, however, was that Isak finally looked like the player Liverpool broke, at that time, the British transfer record to seal an acrimonious transfer from Newcastle United last summer.

Throw in the added bonus that Bradley Barcola showed flashes of devastating pace in a 26-minute debut display after his £123m arrival from Paris St-Germain, and this was a night that ticked every box for Iraola and Liverpool.

Even Barcola's bow, however, was overshadowed by Isak.

The Sweden striker looked a lost soul in his first season at Liverpool, arriving out of condition after downing tools to secure his move from Tyneside, then troubled by injuries as he gave the impression of being the most expensive vanity purchase in British football history.

He was outshone by fellow striker Hugo Ekitike, his statistics stark as he suffered along with many others in an astonishing decline amid Liverpool's dismal title defence that led to Slot's sacking only a year after he lifted the Premier League trophy.

Isak played 22 games encompassing 1,033 minutes, scoring four goals at a rate of one every 258 minutes. He played 14 games in the Premier League totalling 703 minutes, scoring only three goals at a rate of one every 234 minutes.

He has already equalled that league tally this season, but it was his demeanour as well as his lethal finishing that will have given Liverpool and Iraola confidence that the Isak code has finally been cracked.

And it was done by utilising Isak at his best - running in behind defenders and pressing with pace. It was what made him such a hot property at Newcastle United, and made everything about his every miserable moment on the pitch with Liverpool last term such a mystery.

It was also done in tandem with Gakpo, who could easily have been back in the north west preparing for Manchester City's game against Coventry City at Etihad Stadium had the move not collapsed.

articles.title: Brayan Rocchio signals start of 'Rocctober' with grand slam, walk-off
articles.summary: Brayan Rocchio found an extra gear at the end of the year in 2024 and 2025. A few days into this September, he launched a grand slam and a walk-off.
articles.body:
CLEVELAND — A couple of baseballs being launched over the wall at Progressive Field , some ensuing fireworks and even the Blue Angels flying overhead all signaled the official beginning of "Rocctober."

The moniker "Playoff Rocchio" was given to Guardians infielder Brayan Rocchio a few years ago when he went on a tear at the plate in the playoffs , hitting .333 with a .906 OPS in 2024 and helping Cleveland advance to the ALCS. It's become a trend.

Last September, he came through with several clutch, season-saving moments as the Guardians tracked down the Detroit Tigers and overcame a historic deficit en route to a trip to the playoffs, including a walk-off home run that clanged off the right field foul pole and officially clinched the division.

This year, Rocchio seems to have seen his shadow early. September and October are instead "Rocctember" and "Rocctober" at Progressive Field.

Best photos from Cleveland Guardians vs. Detroit Tigers series

On Sept. 4, in the first game of a doubleheader against the Tigers, Rocchio stepped to the plate with the bases loaded and Cleveland trailing 6-2. He drilled a grand slam to tie it.

Later, in the ninth inning, he finished the job by belting a no-doubt, walk-off home run over the left-field wall.

At one point, the Guardians had trailed that game 6-1 before Rocchio nearly single-handedly willed Cleveland to a win, which could be key in the divisional and wild card races.

"Especially when it's a clutch situation and he's up, we believe it's going to happen," Guardians reliever Erik Sabrowski. said. "And it happened today."

Cleveland Guardians photo of the day: Best images from each 2026 game

What is 'Playoff Rocchio' or 'Rocctober'?

Three years in a row now, once the calendar flips to September and then October, Rocchio has seemingly discovered a knack for coming through in the biggest moments of not only that game, but the entire season.

"I think he's got the gene, man," pitcher Slade Cecconi said. "Ever since I've been here, it's like every time, it's unbelievable what he's able to do. I also know he does so much mental prep work. I see him with his headphones on, he has all sorts of stuff to prepare his mind.

"And when you take care of that, those big situations, [they have more intense focus] with a guy that's prepared."

Although it felt like he made every big play for the Guardians last September en route to a playoff berth, Rocchio still posted an OPS under .700 for the month. It was far from a perfect stretch of baseball. And to begin this September, Rocchio was 0-for-6.

But, when the Guardians were at their biggest time of need, he showed up with a grand slam and a walk-off home run, as if the Blue Angels flying overhead acted as a Batsignal.

"It's been pretty cool to see Rocc late in the season the last three years," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. "We just got to keep him going and encouraging him."

articles.title: FIA's Court of Appeal responds to Flavio Briatore bias allegations
articles.summary: The FIA's International Court of Appeal issued a statement in response to Alpine executive Briatore's claims one of its judges in the Monaco GP case had McLa...
articles.body:
The International Court of Appeal defended and clarified the appointment of its judges in the Monaco Grand Prix appeal amid allegations by Alpine boss Flavio Briatore that one of the judges had ties to McLaren .

The International Court of Appeal, which runs independently of the FIA, is the highest court judging over motorsport related matters and was called into action when McLaren and Red Bull appealed against the stewards' decision to rescind Alpine driver Pierre Gasly 's Monaco Grand Prix penalties.

Gasly was one of several drivers incorrectly penalised in Monaco for pitlane speeding, initially losing his podium before Alpine launched a successful right of review procedure. But as other drivers had already served their penalties, unlike Gasly, they could not get their penalties rescinded, with McLaren and Red Bull launching an appeal.

The ICA agreed with the appellants and reinstated Gasly's penalties, frustrating the Frenchman and his Alpine squad. But the team's top boss Briatore took matters further when he launched an explosive rant during the Italian Grand Prix press conference , questioning the integrity of the panel because one judge was purported to have links with McLaren.

The judge in question, Filippo Marchino, served as CEO of the One Drop Foundation, a charity founded by Cirque du Soleil impresario Guy Laliberte. In that capacity, the charity was once gifted several McLaren road cars by late McLaren shareholder Mansour Ojjeh, for the purpose of raising money for the charity via auction. Briatore also referenced an event by McLaren Special Operations in Beverley Hills in 2018, where Marchino appeared as a speaker, an event unrelated to the F1 team.

Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari, Andrea Stella, McLaren, Flavio Briatore, Alpine

The FIA's International Court of Appeal has issued a statement in response to Briatore's explosive allegations, explaining the panel of judges was put together in accordance with its judicial procedures.

"The FIA Courts are aware of public comments questioning the independence and impartiality of the judges of the panel that decided Case ICA-2026-06-07-08-09," the ICA commented, referring to the McLaren and Red Bull appeal.

"The FIA Courts wish to make clear that the appointment and participation of the judges in that case, like for any other case, were conducted in accordance with the applicable FIA judicial procedures and usual practice, which are inspired by the highest standards like the IBA Guidelines on Conflicts of Interest in International Arbitration.

"All judges are elected by the FIA General Assemblies, some of them upon proposition of a group of at least five F1 teams in accordance with the FIA statutes. They are all subject to the independence and confidentiality requirements contained in the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, make annual disclosures of interests to the FIA compliance officer, and sign a specific declaration of independence for each particular case in consideration of the issue at stake and the parties involved, which is served to the parties."

Lando Norris, McLaren, Pierre Gasly, Alpine

The ICA said there were no objections to the composition of the panel before the appeal hearing started, and explained why it is keen to appoint judges with different backgrounds.

"At both the beginning and conclusion of the hearing, the parties were invited to raise any issue concerning the proceedings or the composition of the court. None did so," the statement continued. "No objection was raised during the hearing concerning the manner in which the court questioned the witness or conducted the proceedings.

"The ICA emphasises the importance of constituting panels with judges from different cultural and geographical backgrounds. This helps ensure that the deliberations and discussions reflect a diversity of legal traditions, perspectives and approaches, further strengthening the fairness, independence, credibility of the process and access to a fair trial."

The ICA added: "A court's decision can leave room for various interpretations and comments as for its legal merits; that is fair and accepted by all the judges. The court is confident in the soundness of the proceedings and the integrity of the judges. The FIA courts remain committed to the independence and impartiality of their judges and to the integrity of the judicial process."
