articles.title: Clarke gave SFA 'a little shove' for new contract
articles.summary: Steve Clarke says he had to cajole the Scottish FA into handing him a new contract as national head coach shortly before the World Cup finals this summer bec...
articles.body:
Steve Clarke says he had to cajole the Scottish FA into handing him a new contract as national head coach shortly before the World Cup finals this summer because he felt the governing body was hedging its bets.

But the 63-year-old insists he nevertheless always planned to resign should he fail to lead Scotland beyond the group stage for the first time.

Speaking for the first time since the tournament in the Americas, Clarke was being interviewed by former Chelsea and Scotland team-mate Pat Nevin at Spartans Community Foundation dinner in Edinburgh.

Asked about his exit from the job despite the four-year contract he signed on the eve of the tournament, and quoted by The Scotsman, he said: "It was never really a change of mind.

"I am quite a complex person. I wanted to control my narrative.

"Obviously we got to March and I hadn't been offered a new contract, which I thought was pretty strange. You start to think are they hedging their bets a little bit, waiting on the tournament in the summer.

"So I did a little bit in the media in March to give the SFA a little shove. We negotiated non-stop from the beginning of April really to the middle of May, just before the Curacao game.

"And I said to them if we don't agree a new contract before we go to the World Cup then I will say I am leaving the job. They panicked a little bit and gave me the new contract.

"It was like drawing teeth trying to get it over the line. But we got it over the line anyway.

"But I always knew in my head that if we did not get out of the group stage then I would probably leave. The only way I would have stayed on is if they had been three fantastic games and they went against you."

Scotland beat Haiti 1-0 but lost by the same score to Morocco before a 3-0 loss to Brazil left them waiting for an unlikely series of results to allow them to progress as one of the better third-place sides.

"We had to stay for four or five days [in Charlotte], the longest four or five days ever just sitting and waiting, knowing you are going home because the goal difference was not good enough," he recalled.

"I knew we needed four points. I got hammered in the media for saying that. Somebody hammered me for saying, 'nah, that's us, we are going home'. But I was right."

Clarke revealed he spoke to several senior players following the Brazil game and sensed that they needed to hear a different voice if they are to make history by reaching the knockout stage at Euro 2028.

Meantime, he spoke to new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli last week to wish him well and believes "even Scotland" cannot fail to qualify given two spots in the finals will be reserved for the best-ranked host who have not qualified as a group winner or runner-up.

articles.title: Aaron Judge Makes Emotional Remark As Possible Return From Injury On 9/11’s 25th Anniversary Looms

articles.body:
It was a seemingly good day for the Yankee nation despite the series-opening loss to the Padres in San Diego, as their team captain, Aaron Judge, took part in on-field batting practice for the first time since landing on the IL on May 31 due to a stress fracture in his right rib. The signs were promising, with many expecting Judge to return to the lineup a week or two before the postseason commences.

Yankees senior writer with MLB, Bryan Hoch , shared what Judge had to say about his potential return timeline while offering his own prediction, unofficially marking September 11, the opening game of the Subway Series against the Mets in the Bronx, as the day Judge could be added to the active hitting lineup.

"If I'm playing or not playing, it's going to be special. It's going to be a big day. That impacted not only a lot of New Yorkers but the whole world and our whole country. … I don't know about playing or not playing, but I'll definitely be there and soaking it all in," Judge said in response to a potential return on 9/11.

During an on-field interview with reporters after his batting practice, Judge also revealed that he had been hitting in the batting cages since the medical team cleared him for baseball activities. Furthermore, the three-time AL MVP said his goal was to resume playing in the Yankees' pinstripes sometime during the next homestand.

Aaron Judge Shuns Minor-League Rehab and Instead Aims to Join the Active Roster

Speaking about the ongoing baseball activities beyond hitting, Judge said he is actively engaged in other aspects of the game to fully prepare for the upcoming homestand against the Rockies and the Mets.

"We're hitting all the baseball stuff. Throwing to bases, throwing, running the bases. Hitting, getting on the field, moving around. I think [we need to] face some live pitching and then I'll get back out there," Judge said via MLB.com .

When asked about a potential minor-league rehab game before being reactivated to the roster, Judge, eager to get back on the field, said he saw no use for it under the current circumstances.

"I don't see a point. Why waste at-bats? They haven't told me they wanted me to do one, so we'll see," Judge said via The Athletic .

As for the Yankees, they are currently just four games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East standings as the race for the division title heats up with just 21 games left in the regular season.

articles.title: Two questions Wisconsin football must answer vs. Notre Dame in Week 1
articles.summary: The Notre Dame Fighting Irish will serve as a litmus test for how well the Wisconsin Badgers can compete.
articles.body:
You won't find many harder tests than what the Wisconsin Badgers have to face in just a few days' time against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish .

However, whether they win or lose, the Fighting Irish will serve as a great litmus test for how well the Badgers can compete ahead of a schedule that will provide several opportunities for winnable games to slowly push them back into the spotlight.

But before they can get to those fixtures, there are two questions that must be answered.

No. 1: What are the offensive improvements?

Last season, against power-conference opposition, the Badgers scored more than 10 points just twice. Combine that with an offense that totaled just 253.1 offensive yards per game (135th-worst in the FBS). While no one is expecting this to be a 500-yard week one showing, will they do enough to keep themselves in the game, or will they continuously stall?

No. 2: How does the kicking situation look?

The Badgers compiled a 63.64% field goal rate in 2025, good for 116th in the nation. With 5th-year kicker Gavin Lahm set to take the mantle this season with zero field goals to his name, his production is unknown, and in a game like this against a team like Notre Dame, three points here and there could make all the difference.

The Washington Commanders fans did not have much to cheer about last season, but their latest food offering is sending fans across the league wild.

Jayden Daniels' injury issues contributed to a hugely underwhelming 5-12 record during the 2025 season in Washington.

A lot more will be expected from the upcoming season, with the Commanders now counting down the years until their stadium move.

The current Northwest Stadium leaves a lot to be desired, but improvements are being put in place to their food and beverage offering.

A new crab-stuffed pretzel has now been unveiled ahead of their opening home game later in the month, which has fans seriously impressed.

NFL fans go crazy over Washington Commanders' latest food offering

Food offerings at sports stadiums often go viral on social media, and this is certainly the case with what the Commanders are cooking up in their kitchens.

Ahead of the new season, the Commanders have shared their $24.99 crab-stuffed pretzel with lemon tarragon crab dip, garlic butter and Parmesan cheese.

To say this has sent fans wild on social media would be a huge understatement.

'Maybe I DO care about attending a commanders game,' replied one fan on X.

'Fire food item wasted on a dumpster fire team,' a fan of another team responded.

Following the dreadful 2025 season, the Commanders are going to need to pull out all of the stops in an attempt to get fans into the stadium this year.

Another fan said: 'Oh my goodness, suddenly I want to go on SNF in Week 8 just for this thing'.

'This could be a game changer!' replied another.

If last season is anything to go by, the Commanders fans could be spending more time at the food stalls than actually watching their team play.

One Eagles fan replied: 'Best thing this franchise has done'.

While another fan said: 'This looks absolutely incredible'.

The Commanders will open their season with two games on the road to NFC East rivals before hosting the Super Bowl champions on 27 September.

articles.body:
Hansi Flick has spoken about Lamine Yamal's absence from training.

These were the German coach's words: "Lamine Yamal took a knock and was in pain. It was better for him to train separately. After training he said everything was fine. He will travel with us and tomorrow we'll see."

The coach also spoke about whether Gabriel Jesus will be available: "He's still not at 100%, but I see him enjoying himself with the ball. He can play a few minutes."

Does he have a better squad than last year?

"I can see how well we press, the work we're doing, the rondos, the possession drills. We'll see at the end of the season whether this squad is better than last year's, but in terms of quality it's top."

"With Ter Stegen and Araujo not being available, it's normal that they voted for him. I chose two because of their importance in the dressing room. I'm happy with the team's choice and with the five overall. We'll need players who can speak up and take responsibility."

"What I can say about him is that he is an incredible professional. He gives everything. He is competitive. I spoke with him about the option of playing at centre-back, which he prefers. We want to help him reach his best level. There are fantastic options in every position, and we decide what is best for the team in each match. The decisions can change. But he works hard and wants to reach his best level."

articles.title: 9/10 duels won: New Liverpool signing shines in Ipswich Town victory
articles.summary: Liverpool Beat Ipswich 2-0 as Isak and Araujo Set Tone for Iraola’s First WinAndoni Iraola has his first win as Liverpool head coach. It came without fuss, a...
articles.body:
Liverpool Beat Ipswich 2-0 as Isak and Araujo Set Tone for Iraola's First Win

Andoni Iraola has his first win as Liverpool head coach. It came without fuss, and largely inside the first 10 minutes.

Alexander Isak scored twice away at Ipswich on Friday night, both created by Cody Gakpo, and that was enough for a 2-0 victory. Simple on paper, deserved in practice. Liverpool were clinical early, then organised when they needed to be. That has been missing too often.

Isak will take the attention because goals decide games and centre-forwards live off moments like these. Gakpo deserves plenty of credit too. Two assists here, after teeing up the Swede against Nottingham Forest last weekend, tells its own story. Liverpool found combinations in the final third and used them ruthlessly.

Araujo justified selection at right-back

The more interesting call came in defence. Iraola changed one player from the side that faced Forest, bringing Ronald Araujo in for Jeremie Frimpong at right-back. It looked a practical decision before kick-off and an obvious one by full time.

Araujo gave Liverpool more defensive certainty. He made a vital interception to stop what looked a certain tap-in, won his duels, competed in the air and helped deliver a first clean sheet since the 2-0 win over Fulham at Anfield in April. For a team that has looked open too often, that matters. 9/10 duels won speaks volumes of his dominant display.

It was not flawless. There was a sliced clearance that handed Ipswich a corner, and a sluggish throw-in that was reversed under the new rules. Fine. Full-backs make mistakes. The point is whether they recover and whether the overall contribution lifts the side. His did.

Defensive control mattered as much as Isak goals

Liverpool looked steadier with Araujo there. He blocked, intercepted and read danger well late on when Ipswich tried to force a way back into the contest. He also drove forward a couple of times, carrying the ball with purpose and showing more composure than many would expect from a defender used in a wide role.

That leaves Iraola with a straightforward dilemma before Atletico Madrid visit next Wednesday in the Champions League. Does he go back to Frimpong, or does he keep the player who made Liverpool harder to play against?

On this evidence, Araujo has earned another start. Isak won the match early. Araujo helped make sure it stayed won.

articles.body:
Chipping in with a goal in VfB Stuttgart's 4-1 rout of 1.FC Köln last night , Ermedin Demirović was a man seeking redemption.

"I set out to regain respect for my name," the striker said, referencing persistent rumours linking him a transfer away from Stuttgart.

"There had been a lot of talk lately, with people saying I was a potential sale. Now I've been able to show that I'm here.

"It meant sleepless nights at home. Even in training camp, a lie was spread that the coach wanted to sell me.

"And I'm not just another player who can't find another club. I wanted to stay here and had great talks with the coach.

"I wanted to continue on this path and not look for an exit," said the 28-year-old who was heavily connected with a Galatasaray move.

Among others, Galatasaray made the Bosnian international a lucrative offer. But Demirovic declined.

Sky Germany even reported several weeks ago that coach Sebastian Hoeneß was open to selling the striker.

However, when asked about it at the time, the 44-year-old coach made a point to say he "was irritated and annoyed by it."

articles.title: Watch 2028 5-star QB and Texas A&M commit's 'perfect ball'
articles.summary: 2028 5-star QB Donald Tabron's highly impressive throw during Cass Tech's Thursday night victory.
articles.body:
Texas A&M's future starting quarterback question will be answered after redshirt junior Marcel Reed , who is entering his second full starting season, departs the program; until then, several names are in the running, including current backup Brady Hart. However, looking past the 2027 season, 2028 five-star QB and Texas A&M commit Donald Trabon III will be in the conversation.

When grading a quarterback this early in his career, the ability to complete 18-yard out routes, requiring NFL-level touch and anticipation, is, and should be, what writers in my position should look for when judging any young signal caller's ceiling. A handful of games into his junior season at Cass Technical, Donald Tabron can seemingly make every throw, especially the out route, and should be considered the top-ranked QB by this time next year.

Ahead of OC Holmon Wiggins' first season at the helm, how the Aggies' passing game will look is still up in the air, but after Tabron committed to Texas A&M over several blue-blood programs, his conversations with Wiggins and QB coach Joey Lynch proves that A&M's offense is quarterback friendly, especially given the talent at wide receiver for years to come just by looking at the 2027 additions.

This week, Cass Tech's Thursday game included one of the best throws you'll see all weekend, as Donald Tabron delivered a perfect throw to receiver Marquell Evans that nearly scored a touchdown, showing off his elite touch in the process. Cass Tech defeated Granville on the road 48-21, and Tabron is expected to make his way back to College Station in the coming weeks.

articles.title: FIA appeal court refutes Briatore impartiality claim
articles.summary: The FIA court of appeal refutes a claim by Alpine boss Flavio Briatore which it says "question the independence and impartiality of the judges".
articles.body:
The FIA court of appeal has refuted a claim by Alpine boss Flavio Briatore which it says "questions the independence and impartiality of the judges" in a case brought by McLaren and Red Bull against the French team.

Briatore claimed on Friday that one of the court of appeal judges in the case that ended with the court re-instating a penalty on Alpine's Pierre Gasly in the Monaco Grand Prix had "links" with McLaren.

The statement by the highest legal authority of motorsport's governing body said that court of appeal judges are "subject to the independence and confidentiality requirements contained in the FIA judicial and disciplinary rules, make annual disclosures of interests to the FIA compliance officer, and sign a specific declaration of independence for each particular case in consideration of the issue at stake and the parties involved".

It added that the parties to the dispute were invited both before and after the hearing "to raise any issues concerning the proceedings or the composition of the court. None did so".

It added: "No objection was raised during the hearing concerning the manner in which the court questioned the witness or conducted the proceedings.

"A court's decision can leave room for various interpretations and comments as for its legal merits; that is fair and accepted by all the judges.

"The court is confident in the soundness of the proceedings and the integrity of the judges.

"The FIA courts remain committed to the independence and impartiality of their judges and to the integrity of the judicial process."

The FIA says the court of appeal "operates independently" of the wider organisation.

On Friday Briatore had said: "One of the judges act like a prosecutor. This is not a big problem. The problem is he's very linked with the McLaren company."

The 76-year-old Italian's claims were based on a charity auction held in California in 2018 which the judge in question had attended and to which he claimed "McLaren gave two, three McLaren cars".

"This was quite unfair," Briatore said. "One of the judges was linked with a team that was protesting us."

Asked why Alpine had not raised objections at the hearing, Briatore said: "We found out, after the meeting, logically, not before, we found out this guy was linked with the McLaren team. This is what I think."

The case against the decision to drop two pit-lane speeding penalties on Gasly in Monaco was brought by both McLaren and Red Bull.

The court of appeal decision demoted Gasly back to seventh place, and promoted three Red Bull drivers and one McLaren driver higher in the points.

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was put back into third place, McLaren's Oscar Piastri to fourth and Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad to fifth and sixth.

Briatore made no reference to Red Bull in his comments.

McLaren have responded angrily to Briatore's comments.

Privately, they reject them out of hand and are angry that what they believe are unfounded claims have been given a public airing in a news conference.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella attended the same news conference in which Briatore made his remarks.

Stella said: "I find that this conference going in this direction is quite insulting for McLaren, for the reputation of a team that deserves a lot of respect.

"And if anybody makes these kind of allegations - which seem quite serious - they are going to have to take the responsibility for what they are saying in a public forum.

"The hearing, the whole International Court of Appeal, was conducted to the highest standards and we should not question this phase as has been done."
authors: Andrew Benson - F1 correspondent in Monza
